When a caller uses this generic `DRM_RADEON_INFO` wrapper for `RADEON_INFO_NUM_BYTES_MOVED`, `RADEON_INFO_VRAM_USAGE`, or `RADEON_INFO_GTT_USAGE`, the kernel writes an 8-byte result; the repo's Radeon shim models those exact requests through a `uint64_t *` in `src/amd/drm-shim/radeon_noop_drm_shim.c:74-78` and has width tests for them in `src/amd/drm-shim/radeon_noop_drm_shim.c:991-1015`. Passing a pointer to this 4-byte stack local lets those valid info queries overwrite adjacent stack data, so the wrapper either needs a 64-bit API/storage path or must be explicitly limited to known 32-bit requests.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse write-only state-token render fds**

When the caller opens the shim render node with `O_WRONLY`, `drm_shim_render_node_open()` preserves that access mode for the per-open state-token memfd and then immediately registers it; this new identity path tries to validate the token by `pread64` through the caller's fd, so the parse fails with `EBADF`, registration returns `ENODEV`, and the open fails even though the code accepts the flag combination and read-only render opens work. The parse needs a readable witness for write-only state-token fds, similar to the existing helper used elsewhere, before closing the carrier fd.
